title: Econ Grandfathering: defaults curator and tenant-safe quant profiles
author: Lena Martinez
description: Context: We frequently ship improved batching/cache defaults and quant profiles that reduce unit cost, but tenants with long-lived pinned defaults or tenant-specific overrides were unexpectedly reharmed by global default rollouts. This PR introduces an 'Econ Grandfathering' curator service that: (1) computes a tenant-safe merged defaults set (batch/caching/kv/quant) by respecting an ordered set of retention rules, (2) produces tenant-scoped quantization compatibility hints (safe precision floor, rollback anchors), and (3) emits a small, auditable plan that can be applied via the existing defaults-as-code CLI. Motivation: reduce incidents from global default churn, enable gradual quant rollouts with tenant-specific safety nets, and provide an operator-facing approval step for edge cases. Summary of changes: - New service: econ/curator with a merge engine and rule evaluator - Defaults schema extension: add "grandfather_since" timestamp and "compat_anchor" metadata to quant profiles - CLI: defaults-curator preview + apply with --dry-run and --audit-log flags - API additions: POST /v1/curator/preview and GET /v1/curator/tenants/{id}/plan - Telemetry: curator.plan_generated and curator.apply_{success,failure} metrics - Tests: unit + integration harness that simulates tenant upgrades and legacy profiles Backwards compatibility: existing defaults and tenant overrides continue to work unchanged unless an operator runs the curator apply action. There is an explicit operator approval flow to avoid silent changes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2026) linked - [x] Unit tests for merge rules - [x] Integration tests against tenant fixtures - [x] CLI integration and audit logs - [x] Telemetry + SLO guardrails - [x] Release note entry (see release_notes) What this is NOT: this PR does not attempt fully automated global rewrites; it is conservative-by-default and surfaces changes for operator approval. Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag (econ.grandfathering.enabled=false by default) 2) run curator preview across a 10% snapshot of tenants, surface plans to PM/SE 3) enable dry-run pipeline and iterate rules 4) opt-in gradual apply with rate limit and automatic rollback on regression metrics (handled in follow-up PR).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial merge engine + ruleset (Lena), schema extension + migrations (Marco), CLI preview/apply plumbing (Priya), api endpoint + integration test harness (Dmitri), telemetry and e2e smoke (Lena).
review_comments: Marco Ruiz (review): The merge rules look solid but I think we should clarify how 'grandfather_since' interacts with tenants that have manual overrides. Please add a unit test that has a tenant override and an older global default and assert override always wins.

Lena Martinez (author): Added test_case_override_wins in tests/econ/test_merge_rules.py and updated rules.py docstring to explain precedence (tenant override > grandfathered default > newer global default).
Priya Nair (review): CLI UX: preview output is quite dense for tenants with many overrides. Could we add a --concise flag that emits only changed keys and a counts summary?

Lena Martinez (author): Implemented --concise mode and updated cli/defaults_curator.py to support both detailed and concise output. Wrote an integration test that asserts concise output < 1KB for large fixtures.
Dmitri Volkov (review): Integration test flaked once on CI due to a timing assumption in the migration test. Please remove fixed sleep and use polling for migration readiness.
Lena Martinez (author): Switched to polling with a 5s timeout in tests/integration/test_curator_preview.py. Re-ran locally and CI green.
release_notes: Introduce Econ Grandfathering curator: preview/apply workflow to safely merge global defaults with tenant overrides and generate tenant-safe quant profiles. Feature gated; operator approval required for apply. Helps prevent cost regressions during default rollouts.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind econ.grandfathering.enabled flag. To run a preview across all tenants: ./rwc defaults-curator preview --snapshot=all --concise; to apply: ./rwc defaults-curator apply --tenant-id=<id> --operator=<email> (requires audit log enabled). Monitor curator.plan_generated and curator.apply_success metrics.
testing_notes: Included deterministic fixtures for tenants with pinned legacy defaults and randomized traffic profile to exercise batching and kv cache paths. Integration harness runs under test harness flag --slow-ci and was used in CI with limited tenant set.
security_considerations: No secret material changes. Audit logs recorded for every apply. Operators must have RBAC role 'defaults-curator:apply' to perform apply. Added unit tests that assert RBAC guard on API endpoint.
follow_up_items: 1) Auto-rollout agent with safety checks (follow-up PR) 2) Expand heuristics to score expected token-cost delta 3) Add UI in console to inspect preview plans
migration_instructions: Apply SQL migration 20260301_add_grandfather_fields.sql; the migration is idempotent. Existing defaults get a null grandfather_since and no compat_anchor until curator runs.
qa_signoff: QA automation: Lena Martinez; QA manual spot-checks by Priya Nair
human_summary: Adds a conservative tool (curator) to compute tenant-safe merges of new cost-saving defaults and quant profiles, providing previewable, auditable plans that operators can approve to avoid surprising tenant regressions.
